ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-acceptance and rolling screening of all directors, general partners, and UBOs against: (i) the Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List administered by Global Affairs Canada under the Special Economic Measures Act; (ii) the Criminal Code s. 83.05 Listed Terrorist Entities list administered by Public Safety Canada; (iii) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; (iv) the OFAC SDN and Sectoral Sanctions Identification Lists, applied as a matter of bank policy because USD-denominated payment rails (Stripe and Shopify Payments) require OFAC compliance; and (v) domestic and foreign PEP databases. Enhanced due diligence is triggered for foreign PEPs, persons from high-risk jurisdictions, and any unusual ownership structure. The LP is not itself a FINTRAC reporting entity for this manufacturing activity, but its formation agent, counsel, and payment processors are reporting entities; the LP maintains an internal AML/CFT manual, EDD triggers, and a five-year record-retention protocol consistent with PCMLTFA and FINTRAC guidance.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BC Registries and Online Services (Corporate Online) for name reservation at https://www.corporateonline.gov.bc.ca and the OneStop Business Registry for limited partnership registration filing at https://www.onestop.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered legal name of a BC limited partnership must be in Roman (Latin-alphabet) script using English or French words, or a combination, and must end with the mandatory designator 'Limited Partnership', 'Société en commandite', or the abbreviation 'L.P.' or 'LP' pursuant to the Partnership Act. Non-Latin branding elements, including CJK ideographs, are not permitted as the registered legal name and must be transliterated into the Roman alphabet; a transliterated or trade-style extra name may be filed with the Registrar if it is distinguishable. Arabic numerals are permitted; the name must be distinguishable from all existing BC and federal corporate names, from other BC limited partnerships, and from names of extraprovincial entities registered in BC.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Professional Engineer (requires licensing under BC professional engineering legislation)
Scandalous, obscene, or misleading terms, or terms implying a greater scope of liability limitation than the LP form actually provides
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Extension: a name reservation may be extended before expiry by submitting a written or online extension request to the Registrar of Companies; the Registrar may grant one additional 56-day period. Rejection appeal: the applicant or its authorized agent may file a formal Name Reconsideration Request with the Registrar of Companies explaining why the proposed name is distinguishable and compliant with the Name Regulation, B.C. Reg. 288/2003; supporting affidavit or documentary evidence of the applicant's goodwill, trade reputation, or prior use may be attached. The Registrar conducts a de novo review of the rejected name. If the reconsideration is denied, the applicant may seek judicial review in the Supreme Court of British Columbia under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, RSBC 1996, c. 241. Submissions should be filed within 14 to 21 days of the rejection notice to preserve position.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Acceptable for statutory registered-office purposes only, provided the arrangement provides a physical municipal street address in British Columbia capable of receiving legal service of process and document handling by a real agent; a P.O. Box or purely postal forwarding arrangement is not acceptable. For tax and substance purposes, a virtual office alone is not sufficient: the Canada Revenue Agency will look to the location of management, personnel, production, and decision-making to determine whether the LP carries on business in Canada and to assess treaty-entitlement and GAAR or anti-hybrid risks; the BC manufacturing context requires actual premises for injection molding and production, so the LP should maintain a physical operating address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk of unannounced on-site physical inspection within the first 12 months: approximately 7-10% aggregate annual likelihood, driven primarily by Canada Revenue Agency administrative audit selection rather than the BC Registrar, which conducts Registrar-led premises inspections in fewer than 2% of LP files. Banking KYC desk reviews carry a materially higher but non-physical follow-up rate of approximately 25%.

incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for British Columbia limited partnerships; capital contributions are fixed by the partnership agreement. Escrow account rules do not apply; general partners must maintain an auditable trust ledger for any subscriber capital held pending formation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the proposed name and registration be approved; the initial general partners shall execute the Statement of Registration and contribute the capital set out in the partnership agreement; the registered office and records office of the limited partnership shall be situated at the address approved, with BC Registries as competent authority; John Doe and Jane Roe are appointed as initial general partners and principal officers, with full authority to open bank accounts, engage legal counsel, and execute any ancillary documents; and all filings required under the Partnership Act, including publication of the intra-provincial registration, be directed to the registered office agent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries Online Name Request Service via Corporate Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS-style search through an authorized service provider or directly on BC Registries online portal. Submit a Name Reservation Request for the proposed limited partnership name, ensuring the corporate designation 'Limited Partnership' or abbreviation 'LP' is included. Select a name that does not create conflict with existing registered entities. Await issuance of Name Reservation Certificate.
required_dossiers: Consent letter from existing name holder if required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused on grounds of confusion or similarity, file a new name request with a materially distinct name or submit a written consent from the holder of the conflicting name. No refund of the name request fee is applicable.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries, Corporate Registry (Victoria office or online service)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and sign Form 12 Statement of Registration under the Partnership Act. Include full legal names and addresses of all general partners (individuals or corporate entities), the BC registered office address, and the agreed capital contribution schedule. Submit the form online via BC Registries or by mail with original signatures. Notarization is required if the form is executed outside Canada or if a filing agent submits on behalf of non-resident partners.
required_dossiers: Consent of each general partner to act as such
Registered office address and records office address in British Columbia
Initial partnership agreement (kept in records, not filed with registry)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a correction notice or requests clarification, file an amended Form 12 with a supplementary affidavit correcting the deficiencies. Respond within 14 days to avoid abandonment of the application; late cure may incur a reinstatement fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Canada Revenue Agency and Provincial Tax Programs
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) Business Registration and BC Corporate Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After issuing the Certificate of Registration for the limited partnership, apply for a federal Business Number (BN) through the CRA New Business Registration portal. Select the entity type 'Partnership.' Register for a GST/HST account if expected taxable supplies exceed the $30,000 threshold. Where applicable, activate a payroll deduction account and an import/export program account for sourcing polymer resins from international suppliers. Also register with BC Corporate Online for any BC provincial tax obligations, including presumed worker classification and provincial health programs if applicable.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the Statement of Registration or Certificate of Registration
Partnership information: fiscal year-end, general partners' names and addresses
Authorized representative declaration and contact details
Bank account opening documentation for the partnership
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA queries the registration, respond through the provided Business Registration enquiry link or call the Business Enquiries line. Resubmit missing documentation within 30 days; corrections can be processed retroactively with minor penalties if filed beyond 90 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the formal partnership agreement approved by the general partners. Record all subscriptions, capital contributions, and profit-sharing ratios. Appoint the principal officers (operations manager, finance officer) and open the corporate minute book containing the pro-forma resolution. Maintain the registered office records and ensure the partnership registers a Statement of Change if the registered office address or general partners change. File an annual report with BC Registries on the anniversary of registration to keep the entity in good standing.

Consent of registered office records agent
Annual Report form for BC Registries
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the annual report or Statement of Change is filed late, BC Registries may impose a late filing penalty and suspend the entity. environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from full Environmental Assessment; subject to registration-only exemption under the Environmental Assessment Act, SBC 2002, c. 43, as the operation is below the Small-Scale Significant Change threshold
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharged to municipal sewer shall meet city by-law limits (suspended solids < 350 mg/L, pH 6–9, oil and grease < 15 mg/L); volatile organic compounds (VOCs) from moulding and annealing processes must not exceed ACGIH threshold limit values; plastic scrap handling shall comply with BC Recycling Regulation for recyclable plastics; disposal of any solvents or waste resins must meet BC Hazardous Waste Regulation requirements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification under the National Fire Code and BC Fire Code; municipal structural loading inspection for injection-moulding machinery; WorkSafeBC occupational health and safety clearance including machine guarding, lockout/tagout procedures, and indoor air-quality monitoring for thermal decomposition products.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency / Agence du revenu du Canada (CRA) for federal income tax, GST/HST, and Business Number registration (portal: https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html); British Columbia Ministry of Finance, Consumer Taxation Branch for the BC Provincial Sales Tax (PST) (portal: https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/taxes/sales-taxes/pst and eTaxBC: https://www.etax.gov.bc.ca/); Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) for customs export declarations and border control.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign entity establishing or operating as a BC limited partnership, the mandatory sequence is: (1) determine whether the partnership is carrying on business in Canada and whether it is a non-resident registrant under the Excise Tax Act; (2) register the limited partnership under applicable BC partnership legislation, or, if formed outside BC, file for extra-provincial registration with the BC Registrar of Companies; (3) apply to the CRA for a 9-digit Business Number (BN) through the CRA business registration service or Form RC1, selecting the GST/HST account code 'RT' where the entity makes taxable supplies in Canada and is not a small supplier; (4) where importing or exporting goods, open a CRA Import/Export 'RM' account and comply with CBSA export reporting requirements through the Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS) or a customs broker; (5) separately register with the BC Ministry of Finance for PST before making any taxable sale of goods or services in British Columbia, using the eTaxBC portal or the applicable BC PST Application for Registration; (6) maintain the BN on all business records, GST/HST returns, PST returns, customs declarations, and third-party payment-processor account details.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not have a US-style 'check-the-box' entity classification regime. A BC limited partnership is, by statute, a fiscally transparent pass-through entity for Income Tax Act purposes: the partnership does not pay income tax, and each partner is separately liable on its allocable share of partnership income, gains, losses, and credits. For GST/HST purposes, however, the partnership is a separate 'person' capable of holding its own GST/HST account, and the GST/HST consequences do not pass through to the partners. Available elections and mechanisms include: (i) voluntary GST/HST registration for a small-supplier partnership under the Excise Tax Act; (ii) the partnership's fiscal-period selection and, where applicable, elections permitted under Canadian partnership taxation rules; (iii) GST/HST group or associated registrant elections for eligibility under sections 273 to 286 of the Excise Tax Act where all members satisfy the conditions, if such an election is commercially appropriate; and (iv) no protective hybrid-mismatch election is provided by the Canada Revenue Agency; Canadian hybrid-mismatch rules apply mechanically to neutralise deduction/no-inclusion outcomes where a foreign jurisdiction treats the same limited partnership as non-transparent, subject to the specific statutory exceptions and carve-outs.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal Goods and Services Tax (GST) / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST) and British Columbia Provincial Sales Tax (PST). BC is a non-participating province, so the federal component is 5% GST and the provincial component is 7% PST; no HST rate applies in British Columbia.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: GST/HST: mandatory federal registration is triggered when the entity carries on commercial activity in Canada and is not a 'small supplier'. The small-supplier threshold is CAD 30,000 in total taxable supplies (including zero-rated supplies) made in Canada in the current calendar quarter and the four immediately preceding calendar quarters. Once that threshold is exceeded, registration is mandatory. BC PST: there is no generally applicable small-supplier threshold; every person who makes taxable sales of goods or services in British Columbia must be registered as a PST vendor before making those sales, unless a specific exemption applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada and British Columbia do not impose real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or a mandatory national e-invoicing clearance regime for GST/HST or PST. Electronic invoicing may be used but must contain the statutory information required by the GST/HST regulations, including the vendor's Business Number and the tax status of the supply. Mandatory electronic filing applies for GST/HST returns where annual taxable supplies exceed CAD 1,000,000; large registrants must also remit certain prescribed payments electronically. GST/HST returns are filed through CRA's GST/HST NETFILE or My Business Account platforms. PST returns are filed electronically through eTaxBC. Export declarations are submitted electronically to CBSA through CERS where a Canadian export declaration is required; this is a customs clearance process, not an indirect-tax fiscal stamping system.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A GST/HST registrant may claim 0% GST/HST on exports of tangible personal property, including custom double-shot PBT mechanical keyboard caps, where the goods are supplied to a purchaser outside Canada and are exported from Canada in accordance with Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act. Zero-rating is available only if the registrant has contemporaneous documentary proof that the goods were delivered to a common carrier or consignee for export, shipped by courier or freight to a destination outside Canada, and were not acquired for use, consumption, or supply in Canada before export. For services, supplies provided to non-residents may be zero-rated under the place-of-supply and non-resident service rules, but services relating to Canadian real property or goods physically situated in Canada remain taxable; for this industrial scope, the key zero-rating event is the physical export of goods. The registrant must also have a valid GST/HST account; voluntary registration is available to a person who only makes zero-rated export supplies so that the person can obtain input tax credits for GST/PST paid on production inputs such as resin, injection moulding services, packaging, courier services, and e-commerce platform fees.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Customs Export Declaration (B13A) or electronic export declaration filed through the CBSA Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS), where required by value or controlled-goods rules
Bill of Lading / air waybill / courier manifest evidencing shipment from Canada to the foreign destination
Commercial invoice showing seller, purchaser, foreign destination, product description, quantity, unit price, declared value, and Incoterms
Packing list correlated with the commercial invoice and shipment
Foreign customs entry or import documentation from the destination country, where obtainable

Inward remittance certificate or equivalent evidence of foreign exchange receipt, such as SWIFT MT103, bank credit advice, or Shopify Payments / Stripe settlement statement identifying settlement of export proceeds
Freight forwarding and carrier proof of delivery, including dock receipts, delivery orders, or courier proof of delivery indicating a destination outside Canada
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess a GST/HST return within the normal four-year reassessment period; the period is unlimited where a return contains a misrepresentation attributable to neglect, carelessness, or wilful default, or where the exporter has committed fraud. If the zero-rated export classification is not substantiated by the documentation bundle, CRA recharacterises the supply as taxable at 5% GST, re-assesses net tax, charges arrears interest and penalties, and may deny or claw back input tax credits previously claimed in respect of the exported goods. The Excise Tax Act imposes penalty exposure of up to 50% of the additional net tax for false statements or omissions made knowingly or under circumstances amounting to gross negligence, and criminal tax evasion prosecutions remain possible in severe cases. The BC Ministry of Finance similarly audits PST vendor documentation and can assess unreported PST plus interest and penalties if goods sold for delivery in BC are incorrectly documented as exports. Exporters must retain the complete proof-of-export file for at least six years and, in practice, for no less than 180 days after shipment should produce the inward remittance evidence to CRA upon demand; failure to do so creates a high risk of retrospective clawbacks, mandatory re-assessments, and penalty exposure.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), governed by the Bank of Canada Act and the Financial Administration Act; payments infrastructure is operated by Payments Canada (Lynx high-value real-time gross settlement system), prudential supervision of chartered banks rests with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI), and AML/CFT supervision of financial entities and money service businesses rests with the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC). Canada has no separate Foreign Exchange Administration or exchange-control licensing body.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully convertible; Canada has accepted IMF Article VIII obligations and does not operate exchange controls on current or capital account transactions. Inward capital contributions, outbound trade settlements, member/profit distributions, and intercompany payments may be made freely in CAD or any permitted foreign currency, and there is no prior-approval or FX-allocation mechanism. Profit-remittance hurdles are therefore tax-documentary, not regulatory-currency: a BC Limited Partnership is fiscally transparent, so non-resident partners remain taxable in Canada on their shares of Canadian-source partnership income (Part I filing; Part XIII applies only for specifically characterized passive payments such as interest, rents, royalties, and management fees), and treaty-reduced withholding requires proper documentation and the NR301/NR302 determination process before the bank executes an outbound distribution.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Statutory requirement: none. Canada imposes no mandatory repatriation window, no surrender ratio, and no obligatory conversion of export proceeds into Canadian dollars. The LP may hold USD or other foreign-currency proceeds in the same Schedule I operating account or in designated foreign-currency accounts. Procedural compliance includes: (i) accurate CBSA export reporting (electronic or B13A) for each commercial shipment of keycaps, (ii) retention of the full sales-shipping file (commercial invoice, packing list, airway bill/bill of lading) for CRA audit, and (iii) automatic FINTRAC reporting by the bank for electronic funds transfers of CAD 10,000 or more, plus completion of the bank's economic-trade-purpose forms for each incoming export wire.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-to-High. Under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) regime administered by the Bank of Canada, digital payment-service providers operating in Canada must be registered and must safeguard end-user funds through an OSFI-regulated Canadian institution. Foreign electronic money institutions (Wise Platform, Payoneer, Airwallex) can be engaged only as secondary payout/card-acquiring rails that settle through a registered PSP; they cannot replace the LP's primary Schedule I operating account, cannot open a client account in Canada without RPAA/FINTRAC registration, and may not unilaterally issue local CAD clearing credentials. Stripe (Canadian-registered PSP/merchant processor) and Shopify Payments are suitable rails for the LP's target 'Shopify_Payments' and 'Stripe' flows, with funds settled in CAD/USD to the LP's bank account; however, importing PBT resin, LC issuance, FX hedging, and partner-capital acceptance all require a chartered bank relationship.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is effectively required for the general partner's authorizing director. The major Schedule I banks accept a FINTRAC-compliant e-KYC/video-identity verification for low-risk non-face-to-face openings, but for a Canadian Limited Partnership they generally require at least one recorded video KYC interview or an in-branch attendance by the GP's director at the initial meeting. The LP must present the certified BC limited partnership registration, partnership agreement, banking resolution, director identification, register of individuals with significant control (ISC register), and proof of address; secondary signatories may complete remote verification after the master relationship is live.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: BC limited partnership without a transparent ultimate-beneficial-owner chain (nominee or offshore GP layers).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified BC Registry search/title page, executed partnership agreement, LP's ISC register, and a control narrative identifying the general partner and every individual or entity owning/controlling 25% or more of the partnership; if any owner is an entity, its own corporate registry extract and ISC register are appended.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incoming capital subscription from non-Canadian partners with undemonstrated source of funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capital call resolution, audited/management financial statements of contributing partners, 90-day bank statements of the sending account, corporate registry documentation of the partner, and a sworn source-of-funds declaration linked to the specific contribution amount routed in the SWIFT MT103.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Commercial mismatch: high-frequency/high-value card-not-present web sales through Shopify/Stripe to global buyers without coherent trade documentation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Device/production narrative for double-shot PBT keycap manufacturing, factory lease/machine invoices, product catalogue, standard terms of sale, Shopify/Stripe merchant-agreement evidence, PCI-DSS attestation, chargeback policy, shipping-integration logs, and CBSA export declarations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained use of foreign-currency accounts and round-trip CAD/USD conversion patterns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Monthly treasury reconciliation showing natural FX exposure (USD sales revenue vs CNY/EUR supply costs), confirmed FX forward/spot contracts, ISDA/credit-support documentation, and the LP's liquidity-clearing policy demonstrating no unlicensed money-service activity or third-party fund transit.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound partner capital must be injected only via SWIFT MT103 from a bank account titled in the contributing partner's own name to the LP's commercial operating account, referencing the LP's exact registered legal name, the BC registration number, and the instruction 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION — [date] — [name of general partner]'. The transfer is routed either to the availability of the beneficiary bank's CAD Lynx settlement or through its USD correspondent/Fedwire channel, and must be classified with the appropriate ISO 20022 purpose code for direct-investment equity flows; the LP must place in the KYC file the capital call, partner accounts, and source-of-funds evidence so that the inward credit is treated as paid-in capital rather than a shareholder loan or taxable advance, and any amount received in USD must be converted or held only in accordance with the LP's documented FX policy.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier disbursements for PBT resin, moulds, tooling, and logistics should be executed by SWIFT MT103 from the LP's Schedule I operating account with the beneficiary name/SWIFT/IBAN exactly matching the registered supplier, the invoice number in field 70, and the ISO 20022 purpose code for goods imports; for high-value orders, an irrevocable at-sight commercial letter of credit governed by UCP 600 should be issued by the bank, with the negotiating/confirming bank in the supplier's jurisdiction enforcing presentation of bill of lading, commercial invoice, packing list, and certificate of origin. All CAD/foreign-currency conversions for disbursements are executed only on instruction from the LP, with the bank's FX desk settling immediately to avoid daylight overdrafts and with the treasury team recording the realised rate against a pre-approved hedging line.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: CAD/USD deliverable FX forward contracts (tenor up to 12 months) under an ISDA/FX master agreement with the Schedule I bank, hedging the USD revenue stream from Shopify Payments, Stripe, and other card-not-present settlement rails.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDF) on CNY/CNH and other Asia-Pacific exotic currencies, net-settled in CAD, to hedge purchases of PBT resin from China/Taiwan where onshore deliverability is unavailable.

Cross-currency or plain-vanilla currency swaps with a regulated Canadian bank for balance-sheet alignment of partner-capital currencies, CAD operating costs, and USD/CNY trade payables, subject to the LP's board approval and documented derivative limit.

stage_5.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 0–590 per year (CAD 0–800); third-party BC registered office and agent services typically cost USD 220–590 (CAD 300–800) annually. The LP may use its own registered office at a BC address at no external cost.
stage_5.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000–12,000 (CAD 7,000–15,000) only if the partnership agreement or a lender contractually requires a certified audit; no statutory audit fee otherwise.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% at entity level (Limited Partnership is fiscally transparent / flow-through under subsection 96(1) ITA); active business income is taxed in the hands of partners. Combined federal + BC general corporate rate applicable to corporate partners: 27.0% (15% federal + 12% BC). For BC individual partners, top combined marginal rate: 53.5%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small Business Deduction (SBD) for CCPC partners: effective combined rate on active business income 11.0% (9% federal + 2% BC), subject to the annual business limit; SR&ED investment tax credits (refundable 35% for eligible CCPCs, non-refundable 15% for others); immediate 100% CCA expensing of qualifying manufacturing machinery and equipment acquired after April 19, 2021 and before 2028; BC provincial SR&ED credit (10% of qualifying BC expenditure) if applicable; no statutory tax holiday for standard manufacturing.
